component_findings.abstraction_ceremony: Recertified level 4 under the current criterion: Reusable abstractions such as types, interfaces/traits/generics or equivalent mechanisms can be declared and consumed without excessive scaffolding. Evidence basis: Manual inspection of the reusable Swift micro (mb00-mb11) and adversarial (ADV-*) programs under template/programs/swift, scored per language_quality.md guidance: idiomatic, production-reasonable Swift, no artificial verbosity or artificial brevity. | Swift core constructs (struct value types with mutating funcs, trailing-closure syntax, string interpolation, range operators, guard/if-let optional binding) let algorithmic logic (mb01 fib, mb04 accumulator loop, mb10 buffered IO/parsing) be expressed compactly without extra helper boilerplate. | Some structural overhead is intrinsic to the language/runtime rather than to workload authoring: conditional import Darwin/Glibc for fflush, mandatory do/try/catch around every Foundation FileHandle call in mb10, and the CommandLine.arguments plus ContinuousClock harness repeated in every micro file, required uniformly by the frozen benchmark harness and not Swift-specific bloat. | Swift standard library has no first-class buffered line writer/reader, only Foundation FileHandle primitives, so mb10 manual 65536-byte buffer flush/read/carry-over loop is longer than the buffered-IO idioms available out of the box in some comparison languages such as Java BufferedWriter/Reader or Go bufio, a real conciseness cost attributable to language/stdlib design. | Type inference reduces line noise versus explicitly-typed languages; no unnecessary copi…

metric.code_efficiency_conciseness.limitations: Comparison-language reprojection requires the preserved paid source evidence plus the historical program/workload/toolchain inputs to match the current shard; mismatches remain misses.
metric.code_efficiency_conciseness.selection_rule: Judge intrinsic mandatory ceremony for the same kinds of ordinary programs. Do not reuse raw LOC/bytes/tokens as the score and do not reward external libraries.

component_findings.consistency_regular_forms: Recertified level 3 under the current criterion: Similar concepts use regular forms with few special-case spellings or context-dependent surface rules. Evidence basis: Manual review of naming, control flow, structuring, and commenting conventions across the same Swift micro and adversarial corpus. | Consistent descriptive naming such as workload, main, parseDecimal, splitLine, Lcg and doc comments on structs and functions aid readability, reflecting normal idiomatic Swift style, not benchmark-specific dressing. | guard-let and optional binding patterns make error and failure paths locally visible and linear rather than deeply nested, a genuine Swift language-design readability strength versus languages requiring nested null checks. | Trailing closure syntax and structured timing APIs such as ContinuousClock read naturally in-line without extra ceremony. | Some readability friction: low-level byte-level parsing required for the frozen IO buffer contract is inherently less readable than string-level APIs, though this constraint is applied identically across languages, not Swift-specific. | mutating func and value-type struct semantics are explicitly marked, aiding reasoning about state mutation compared to languages where mutation is implicit.
